text:
maria: Heads-up — ran a large-scale perf sweep for fp8 mixed kernels against baseline fp16. Found consistent NaN/Inf spikes when KV cache length crosses ~1024 tokens. Repro on dev-gpu-2. Profiling snippet below.

maria: profiler dump (trimmed):
```
kernel_select_counts: { fp8_mixed: 1842, int8: 0, fp16_stable: 132 }
p99_latency_ms: 78 -> 210 (during spike)
gpu_mem_mb: 15200
nan_count: 372 (all in attention softmax / kv mul)
sequence_lengths: median=256, max=2048
kv_cache_evictions: 0
batch_shape: [1, 8, 64] (continuous batching)
```

maria: notes: spikes correlate with long-running KV cache use + continuous batching (many different seq lengths queued).

raj: ugh. thanks for the dump. first thought: fp8 kernels are faster but more fragile for accumulation/attn matmuls. Might be scale overflow in KV quantization or softmax numeric instability.

kevin: agree. two likely vectors: 1) quantization scale mismatch when caching keys/values across different batch shapes, 2) rounding accumulation when we repeatedly quantize/dequantize KV on every request and keep reusing cached quantized tensors.

anya: any chance this is a batching heuristic regression? last week we changed the batch coalescer to prioritize throughput over shape homogeneity. Could be mixing short+long and causing quantized rescaling errors.

maria: yup, coalescer changed. When a long req is coalesced with many short ones we do per-request calibration on the fly (fast approximate) -> that is probably using single global scale per-tensor, not per-channel.

raj: mitigation ideas: fallback policy to fp16_stable kernel if NaNs detected OR when kv_length > threshold. Also consider re-quantizing KV cache to fp16 for keys older than X tokens.

kevin: would prefer smoother approach: smoothquant + per-channel scaling for weight-activations. Smoothquant reduces range amplification and tends to avoid Inf. Offline calibration takes a few secs but maybe we can cache calibration tables per model version.

maria: experimented with quick clipping: clip activations at 8*stddev before quantizing -> reduced NaNs to 3 across same run but increased p99 by ~6ms. Throughput still better than fp16, though spikes are muted.

anya: operationally, fallback on NaN detection is cheap: if kernel returns NaN set a per-connection flag to use fp16 for next N requests. But we need to avoid flapping. Maybe exponential backoff for fp8 retries.

raj: yes. Proposed patch:
```
- add runtime flag --prefer-robust-kernel (default off)
- on kernel NaN/Inf detection: record failure_count++, if failure_count>2 => switch to fp16_stable for 5min
- also emit metric runtime.quant.kernel_fallback{model,region}
```

kevin: also add a calibration CI test: run small sample with seq_len=2048 and ensure no NaNs for fp8 mixed; if NaNs -> block merge. We should run both online quick calibration and offline full per-channel calibration.

maria: also found kv cache overflow pattern: when we store quantized KV and later multiply with fp16 activations we get mismatched scales. The KV rescale path currently assumes homogeneous scales. Need per-head scaling or store scale metadata with cached tensors.

raj: good call. store scale per cached block and use that during matmul. That avoids re-quantizing on read in many cases and prevents double-scaling errors.

anya: cost/benefit? storing per-block scales adds ~8 bytes per head per cached block. negligible relative to tensor size.

maria: benchmark after two quick fixes (clip + per-block-scale in cache):
```
p99 before: 210ms
p99 after: 92ms
nan_count: 372 -> 1
throughput delta vs fp16: +1.6x
```

kevin: nice. But still want smoothquant path in model prep: smoothquant alpha=0.5 reduced p99 further and eliminated the lone NaN in 3/3 runs. Perf hit small. We should add model onboarding step: try smoothquant and compare quality/perf.

raj: operational rollout plan:
- quick patch: clip activations + store per-block scale + naive fp8->fp16 fallback logic (short-term) (owner: maria, PR today)
- medium: CI calibration test + instrumentation + metrics (owner: kevin)
- long: model onboarding pipeline integrates smoothquant, per-channel calibration, auto-kernel policy (owner: raj)

anya: add a runtime flag to prefer homogeneous batching for fp8 (i.e., don't coalesce long with short) — probably reduce throughput slightly but increase stability. Config: batch_coalesce_homogeneity_threshold.

maria: will open an issue and link perf logs. my quick-PR will include a small unit test reproducer.

infra-bot: Deployed maria/fp8-clip-fallback branch to staging at commit sha=0f4b2a.

kevin: after staging run, we should run a stress test: 1000 concurrent warm sessions with varying seq lengths up to 2048 and monitor kernel_fallback metrics.

maria: opened ticket RW-3245 with reproducer and attached profiler output. assigning to raj + kevin.

raj: thanks. I'll take the medium/long items. kevin can you own calibration CI?

kevin: yep. I'll write a small harness that runs offline per-channel calibration and emits a pass/fail and calibration artifacts to model store.

anya: also add alerting: if kernel_fallback rate > 0.5% in prod for a model, auto-roll to previous stable model and page.

maria: one more note — when we re-quantize KV cache to fp16 as fallback, we must preserve kv_cache indexing to avoid invalidation storms. Might need a shallow version stamp on cache entries.

raj: agreed. we'll version entries and keep GC for old-stamped entries.

maria: thanks all, will follow up with PR link and staging results later today. :thumbsup:
